layers.note: Local in the south Puget Sound lowlands, in small clonal groves at prairie and wetland edges.

moisture.note: Moist ground at the edges of wetlands and prairies.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Very cold winters borne: coldest-month means from about −25 °C (gone by −35 °C), as across the boreal forest.

hard_freeze_c.note: Among the hardiest: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Short, cool summers suffice: warmest-month means from about 11.5 °C, the tree line's warmth, up to about 22.5 °C; gone below 9 °C and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 700.

degree_days_5.note: A short growing season suffices: about 450 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 200.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.35, gone by 0.25.

summer_rain.note: No limit in its range: summer-dry coasts to continental summer rain.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Quaking aspen spans North America from Alaska to Newfoundland and south in the Rockies to Mexico (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
